title: Working with JSON and Fetch API — Project

pool_config.pool_brief: Build an interactive data-fetching application that loads, displays, and handles errors with real API data. Your solution must use: JSON.parse and JSON.stringify, fetch() with .then() and .catch(), a response.ok check that throws on error, rendering fetched data to the DOM, and a loading/error state indicator. All variables must use const or let.

projects.title: Andela Developer Directory
projects.scenario: Build a developer directory that fetches user profiles from a public API, displays them as cards, handles errors gracefully, and demonstrates JSON round-trips.
requirements: Use fetch to load users from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users' with .then() chaining
Check response.ok before parsing; if not ok, throw an Error with the status code
Render each user as a card in the DOM showing name, email, and company name (use map + innerHTML or createElement)
Add a 'Load Users' button with a click handler that triggers the fetch; show a 'Loading...' state while fetching
Add a 'Trigger Error' button that fetches a non-existent URL; display the error message in a red error box using .catch()
Demonstrate JSON.stringify by converting the first user object to a formatted JSON string and displaying it in a <pre> element
Demonstrate JSON.parse by parsing a hardcoded JSON string into an object and logging its properties

files.content: Andela Developer Directory

projects.title: Flutterwave Transaction Viewer
projects.scenario: Build a transaction viewer that fetches post data from a public API (simulating transactions), displays them, handles errors, and demonstrates JSON operations.
requirements: Use fetch to load posts from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts?_limit=8' with .then() chaining
Check response.ok before parsing; if not ok, throw an Error with the status code
Render each post as a transaction card in the DOM showing title and body (use map + innerHTML or createElement)
Add a 'Load Transactions' button with a click handler that triggers the fetch; show a 'Loading...' state while fetching
Add a 'Trigger Error' button that fetches a non-existent URL; display the error message in a red error box using .catch()
Demonstrate JSON.stringify by converting a transaction object to formatted JSON and displaying it in a <pre> element
Demonstrate JSON.parse by parsing a hardcoded JSON string representing a transaction and logging its properties

files.content: Flutterwave Transaction Viewer

projects.title: Cowrywise Investment Feed
projects.scenario: Build an investment feed that fetches data from a public API, displays investment-style cards, handles fetch errors, and demonstrates JSON serialization.
requirements: Use fetch to load data from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts?_limit=6' with .then() chaining
Check response.ok before parsing; if not ok, throw an Error with the status code
Render each item as an investment card in the DOM (use map + innerHTML or createElement)
Add a 'Load Feed' button with a click handler; show a 'Loading...' state while fetching
Add a 'Trigger Error' button that fetches an invalid endpoint; display the error in a styled error box using .catch()
Demonstrate JSON.stringify with indentation (2 spaces) by displaying the first item as formatted JSON
Demonstrate JSON.parse by converting a JSON string to an object and displaying its properties in the DOM

files.content: Cowrywise Investment Feed

projects.title: Moniepoint Customer Lookup
projects.scenario: Build a customer lookup tool that fetches user data from a public API, displays profiles, handles lookup failures, and demonstrates JSON parse/stringify.
requirements: Use fetch to load a single user from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1' with .then() chaining
Check response.ok; if not ok, throw an Error with the status
Render the user profile in the DOM showing name, email, phone, and company
Add a 'Lookup Customer' button that fetches the user; show 'Searching...' loading state
Add a 'Bad Lookup' button that fetches a non-existent user ID (/users/999); display the error using .catch()
Demonstrate JSON.stringify by displaying the fetched user as a formatted JSON string
Demonstrate JSON.parse by parsing a hardcoded customer JSON string and rendering it in the DOM

files.content: Moniepoint Customer Lookup

projects.title: Opay Merchant Activity Feed
projects.scenario: Build a merchant activity feed that fetches comment data from a public API, displays it as an activity log, handles errors, and demonstrates JSON operations.
requirements: Use fetch to load comments from 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/comments?_limit=10' with .then() chaining
Check response.ok before parsing; if not ok, throw an Error with the status code
Render each comment as an activity entry in the DOM showing name, email, and body text
Add a 'Load Activity' button that triggers the fetch; show 'Loading activity...' state
Add a 'Trigger Error' button that fetches an invalid URL; display the error using .catch()
Demonstrate JSON.stringify by formatting the first comment as JSON and displaying it
Demonstrate JSON.parse by parsing a hardcoded JSON activity string and logging its fields

files.content: Opay Merchant Activity Feed

descriptors.full: fetch used with proper .then() chain; response.ok checked and error thrown if false; .catch() handles both network errors and thrown errors; data parsed with response.json()
descriptors.partial: fetch used but response.ok not checked, or .catch() missing
descriptors.none: No fetch call or entirely broken fetch chain

descriptors.full: JSON.stringify used with indentation to display formatted JSON; JSON.parse used to convert a string to an object; both operations demonstrated with correct output
descriptors.partial: One of parse/stringify used correctly, the other missing or incorrect

descriptors.full: Fetched data rendered to the DOM as cards/entries; loading state shown during fetch; error state displayed in styled element; UI updates correctly for all states
descriptors.partial: Data rendered but loading or error state missing
descriptors.none: Data only logged to console; no DOM rendering

descriptors.full: const/let used; event listeners attached correctly; render logic separated into a function; no var; code handles all three states (loading, success, error)
descriptors.partial: Minor issues — render logic not separated, or one state missing
descriptors.none: var used, no state handling, or fetch logic is broken
